title: It didn’t feel like pride…
paragraphs:
It didn’t feel like pride…
It felt like purpose.
And that’s why it almost destroyed you.

You weren’t rebelling.
You were serving.

You weren’t running from God.
You were doing things for God.

And you didn’t notice…
until the presence faded.
Here’s the part no one says out loud:

You can be gifted…
and still be drifting.

You can be anointed…
and still be empty.

You can be used publicly…
and be dying privately.
Because pride doesn’t always look like arrogance.
Sometimes it looks like competence without dependence.

You started moving ahead of God…
while still using His name.

People still clapped.
Doors still opened.
Opportunities kept coming.
This is where pride hides best:

Not in rebellion…
but in self-sufficiency dressed as gifting.
Scripture doesn’t stay silent about this.
“Your heart became proud on account of your beauty, and you corrupted your wisdom because of your splendor.” — Ezekiel 28:17
Some scholars interpret this as referring to the fall of a powerful king, while others see a deeper reflection of a spiritual fall.
Either way, the warning is clear:

The very thing God gives…
can become the very thing that replaces Him.

Your voice.
Your leadership.
Your influence.
Your platform.
None of those are the problem.
The problem is when the gift becomes your source… instead of God.
And here’s the tension most people avoid:

God may still allow fruit…
even when your roots are drying up.
But to save you from yourself.

The strength fades.
The clarity shakes.
The fire feels distant.
Here’s the truth that breaks pride:
Jesus never relied on His own power.
“The Son can do nothing by Himself; He can do only what He sees His Father doing…” — John 5:19
If Jesus—the Son of God—chose dependence…
What makes us think gifting is enough?
This is where the Gospel confronts us.
You and I don’t just struggle with weakness.

We want to serve God…
while still being in control.
“I don’t need to go back to the secret place.”
You were never meant to carry it.
Because Jesus didn’t come to upgrade your gifting.
He came to crucify your pride.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
It means God Himself will resist the one who refuses to surrender.
But because He refuses to let pride destroy you.

Grace is not given to the gifted.
Grace is given to the humble.
You don’t need to prove anything anymore.
You don’t need to carry the weight of being “used.”

No one sees.
No one applauds.
No one affirms.
This is the invitation of the Gospel:
Redemption says: “I will use you—My way.”
“Apart from Me you can do nothing.” — John 15:5
So if you feel that emptiness…
That hidden exhaustion behind your gifting…
“Lord… I made the gift my source.”
“Teach me to depend on You again.”
Because God doesn’t discard the gifted.
And the version of you that walks in humility?
Than anything pride could ever produce.
If this exposed something in you…
